name: encoding_rs
workload: Decoding/encoding real-world text samples in many languages (English, CJK, Arabic, etc.) between UTF-8/UTF-16/legacy encodings, x86_64 Haswell with SSE2, ICU 55 as shipped by Ubuntu 16.04
claimed_speedup: 7.23x faster decode and 7.00x faster encode than ICU for English UTF-8<->UTF-16; 1.6x-3.9x faster for most other languages; some cases (UTF-16LE/BE) 0.30x-0.32x (slower than ICU)
compiler_and_flags: Rust, tested with and without explicit SSE2 enabled
hardware: x86_64 (Haswell); also tested on ARMv7/ARMv8 (Raspberry Pi 3)
stars_or_usage: 467 stars; core dependency of Firefox/Gecko and Servo (WHATWG Encoding Standard implementation)
tradeoffs: API differs from ICU (Rust-native, WHATWG Encoding Standard semantics rather than ICU's broader encoding conversion API); no arbitrary encoding support, only WHATWG-listed encodings
caveats: Benchmark is first-party (author's own blog, Nov 2016), against ICU 55 (a decade-old ICU release built by Ubuntu's toolchain, not necessarily representative of current ICU perf); author explicitly notes ICU's build flags/compiler may differ from ICU as used in real browsers; some directions (UTF-16LE/BE) are slower than ICU, not uniformly faster.
found_via: WebSearch: "encoding_rs faster than ICU benchmark UTF-8 Rust"

name: utf8_range (SIMD Range-based UTF-8 validator)
baseline: Lemire's SIMD UTF-8 validator (github.com/lemire/fastvalidate-utf-8, the algorithmic ancestor incorporated into simdutf)
workload: Byte-by-byte SIMD UTF-8 string validation of UTF-8-demo.txt and synthetic buffers of varying sizes (32B-1M), comparing naive/lookup/Lemire/range/range2 algorithms on NEON (armv8a) and SSE4 (Xeon E5-2650)
claimed_speedup: range2 algorithm reaches 1579.85 MB/s vs Lemire's 1198.50 MB/s on NEON (armv8a, ~32% faster) on the demo text, with a consistent ~20-32% edge across sizes; on SSE4 (E5-2650) range2 is roughly at parity with Lemire (3986.13 vs 3954.74 MB/s on demo text) and sometimes slower on small buffers (e.g. 32 bytes: 2173.02 vs 2890.52 MB/s)
compiler_and_flags: gcc-7.3 (per original cyb70289/utf8 README; flags for current protobuf-bundled build not confirmed)
hardware: SSE4 test: Intel Xeon E5-2650; NEON test: unspecified ARMv8-A chip ("armv8a")
stars_or_usage: Bundled into Google Protocol Buffers (72k+ stars) as third_party/utf8_range; also used by ScyllaDB; originally developed in the now-archived protocolbuffers/utf8_range (21 stars) and cyb70289/utf8
tradeoffs: C API only, no C++ RAII wrappers beyond what protobuf itself provides; win over Lemire's algorithm is ARM-specific, not universal across x86
caveats: Exact ARM CPU model not stated (only ISA family "armv8a"), so ARM result falls short of full Tier A reproducibility; on x86 SSE4 the advantage over Lemire's algorithm is within noise and sometimes reversed for small inputs, so "faster" claim should be read as ARM-specific, not a universal win over the simdutf lineage.
found_via: WebSearch: "utf8_range google protobuf faster UTF-8 validation SIMD", then read https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/third_party/utf8_range/README.md

name: SimdUnicode
workload: UTF-8 validation of Twitter.json plus synthetic strings in Arabic, Chinese, emoji, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Latin, Russian; measured on Intel Ice Lake and Apple M2
claimed_speedup: Up to 13x faster on emoji-heavy content on Ice Lake; 2.4x faster on Twitter.json on Ice Lake (29 GB/s vs 12 GB/s); on Apple M2, 1.5x-4.1x faster, with 1.8x on Twitter.json (25 GB/s vs 14 GB/s)
compiler_and_flags: .NET SIMD (Vector512 on x64, NEON on ARM); exact .NET SDK version and build flags not confirmed
stars_or_usage: 49 stars; flagged in dotnet/runtime issue #103781 as a candidate replacement for the BCL's own validator
tradeoffs: C#/.NET only; baseline being beaten is .NET's own SIMD-accelerated validator (already fast), not ICU/std::codecvt/simdutf directly, though it is the same simdutf-family algorithm ported to C#
caveats: Benchmark is by the simdutf/Lemire team itself (first-party), published on the author's blog rather than in an independently reviewed venue; exact .NET version/build flags not confirmed by this search.
found_via: WebSearch: "simdutf/SimdUnicode .NET faster than Encoding.UTF8 benchmark", then read https://lemire.me/blog/2024/06/20/validating-gigabytes-of-unicode-strings-per-second-in-c/

name: go-simd/utf8
workload: UTF-8 validation and rune counting on ASCII and mixed multibyte text buffers (16 KiB-1 MiB) using the Lemire-Keiser lookup-based SIMD algorithm, run on amd64 (AVX2) and s390x (IBM z15, VXE2) real hardware
claimed_speedup: 19.07x faster than stdlib on amd64/AVX2 (5,940 MB/s vs 312 MB/s) for validation; ~4.6x faster rune counting; on IBM z15 (s390x): 1.96x (ASCII 16 KiB), 1.73x (ASCII 1 MiB), 10.4x (mixed/multibyte 1 MiB), 9.5x (rune count 1 MiB)
compiler_and_flags: Go 1.26.4, AVX2 on amd64, VXE2 on s390x
hardware: AMD EPYC 7763 (amd64, GitHub Actions); IBM z15 (s390x, real hardware, measured 2026-07-03)
stars_or_usage: 0 stars; new project with CI-driven, reproducible cross-architecture benchmark suite (.github/workflows/bench.yml)
tradeoffs: Pure-ASCII input is actually slower per-cycle than stdlib without a pre-scan short-circuit (mitigated by an ASCII fast path achieving 1.7-2.0x); ppc64le numbers are LLVM-mca cycle-model estimates, not measured on real silicon.
caveats: Very new/low-usage project (0 stars) so treat as an early-stage result; ppc64le figures are simulated, not hardware-measured, and are excluded from the speedup figures above.
found_via: WebSearch: "Go simd utf8 validation faster than encoding/utf8 stdlib benchmark", then read https://github.com/go-simd/utf8
